clue.text: Reach conclusion in essay with it

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the conclusion inside the essay

parts.note: an essay is an attempt
to reach a conclusion is to end

explanation.surface: Advice to a student on finishing an essay that is up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' here is the old sense of an attempt rather than a school composition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'With it' is an informal idiom for fashionable, the same sense as the adjective trendy.

clue.text: Misplaced wit, lacking seriousness in period of decline

indicators.note: misplaced letters are out of their proper spots, so they are put in a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters
light means not serious

explanation.surface: Humour that has gone flat and frivolous in someone's later years.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is figuratively the final stage of something, its waning years, like the fading light at dusk.

clue.text: Habitual character of group in quiet hospital

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following words, spread across them

parts.note: the tail of the first word joins the head of the second

explanation.surface: The usual atmosphere among staff on a calm hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Quiet and hospital tempt you to abbreviate them to P or SH and H, but the answer is simply sitting in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values of a community or institution.

clue.text: Noble endlessly expected to join game with kings and queens

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at noon
chess pieces include kings and queens

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is expected to sit in on a card game with royal cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Kings and queens suggest cards, but the game is chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a woman of high rank in the peerage, so a noble in the noun sense.

clue.text: City cut to pieces by conflict

parts.note: a war is a conflict
to saw is to cut something up

explanation.surface: A city reduced to ruins in a war, as the Polish capital was in 1944.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads its pieces back to front: the cutting comes second in the answer, after the conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital of Poland, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Isn't inserting pages –- nothing is put in

indicators.note: something inserting other material takes it into its middle, so the outer word wraps the rest

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
pp is the abbreviation for pages
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: A complaint that a document lacks its pages and has nothing added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in' looks like more instructions to insert, but it is the definition, in the sense of putting someone into a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to install them in a post, as when a government is put in.

clue.text: Heartless cad no rule's reformed?

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is removed
reformed means made over into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word cad with its centre taken out
the remaining fodder letters

explanation.surface: Is a callous rogue who follows no rules ever reformed?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a heartless cad who obeys no rule describes a rogue, and the question mark flags the double reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest, unprincipled person, exactly a heartless rule-breaking cad.

clue.text: Reason to include one piece of writing that's fanciful

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, something fanciful

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so the outer word takes the rest inside

parts.note: the why of something is its reason
I is the Roman numeral one
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: A justification for including a fanciful essay in a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsy is playful, quaint fancy, the quality of something fanciful or capricious.

clue.text: Last drink that may go to one's head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the final alcoholic drink before bed

definitions.text: that may go to one's head
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cap worn in bed, which sits on the head

explanation.surface: A final drink of the evening that makes the drinker tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to one's head' suggests alcohol making you giddy, but the second meaning is literal: a cloth cap pulled on at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bedtime tipple and the old-fashioned sleeping cap worn on the head.

clue.text: Quietly move on, for example

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, quietly
to reposition something is to move it

explanation.surface: An instruction to slip away quietly, perhaps a stage direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move on' reads as one phrasal verb, but the split comes after move: on is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: On is a word showing position relative to a noun, so it belongs to that part of speech.

clue.text: Experts add it for your health!

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Specialists recommend something as good for your health.
explanation.walkthrough: PROSIT is a German and Latin drinking toast, so the exclamation mark matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a toast wishing good health, Latin for 'may it benefit', like saying cheers.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval during this speech is stated twice

indicators.note: something happening during an event lies within it, so the answer is found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second
a playful nod: the sound of the answer is a drawn-out S, as in the doubled 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone booing a speaker after a point is repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the words this and speech; the closing phrase adds colour, hinting at the hissing sibilants of a twice-said 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience hisses to show it disapproves, so a hiss is a sound of displeasure.

clue.text: Observer, I heard, distorted its news

indicators.note: what is heard is what is spoken, so the word I is taken by its sound

parts.note: the pronoun I sounds like the organ of sight

indicators.note: something distorted is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A bystander complains that a report has twisted the news.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is someone who saw an event, an onlooker or observer of it.

clue.text: Deadly gunman –- note small nose

parts.note: a sharp is a musical note raised a semitone
S is the abbreviation for small
hooter is British slang for nose

explanation.surface: A description of a killer with a little nose, as in a wanted poster.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is informal British slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpshooter is an expert marksman, a gunman whose aim is deadly accurate.

clue.text: Outlaw's to commit crime with head covered

parts.note: robbing is committing a crime
in a hood describes a covered head

explanation.surface: A criminal pulls up a hood to hide his face before a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures any masked thief, but the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the outlaw of English legend who robbed the rich to give to the poor.

clue.text: Rally in Rome initially extremely supportive of Italian author

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece supporting another sits underneath it, so it comes later
initially points to the beginning of a word, so only its opening letter counts

parts.note: first letter of Rome
Umberto Eco, Italian novelist
very and extremely are synonyms

explanation.surface: A literary gathering in Rome with very enthusiastic backing for an Italian novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Umberto Eco wrote The Name of the Rose; in a down clue the supporting piece sits below his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a recovery in strength, as when prices or a patient pick up again.

clue.text: Recreational facility in between two vessels

indicators.note: between places one piece in the middle, with one vessel on each side of it

parts.note: first vessel: a bowl is a dish
taken as written, placed between the two vessels
second vessel: a galley is a ship

explanation.surface: A leisure centre squeezed between two ships in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In between' looks like one phrase, but IN is a piece that sits between the two vessels; one vessel is a dish, the other a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling alley is a venue for the game of tenpin, a place of recreation.

clue.text: Craftily get around monarch in dispute

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed outside the other

parts.note: to wangle something is to obtain it by cunning
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Manoeuvring cleverly round a king during a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangle is a long, noisy argument, a synonym of dispute.

clue.text: Person who gathers what's abandoned in general

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Someone who collects things left behind in general.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the definition well, since such a person collects leftovers, but 'abandoned' is the signal to shuffle the letters of general.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner collects grain left in fields after harvest, or gathers information bit by bit.

clue.text: Second slow movement that may be hard to interpret

definitions.text: that may be hard to interpret
definitions.note: the answer is a noun, writing that may be hard to read

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a crawl is a very slow pace

explanation.surface: A slow second movement of a symphony that is difficult to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow movement' suggests music, as in an adagio, but it means a creeping pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is messy, hurried handwriting, the kind of script that is difficult to read.

clue.text: View Surrealist works by European producing shock

parts.note: to scan is to look over
paintings by Salvador Dali, the Surrealist
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Looking at Surrealist paintings by a European artist proves shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To scandalise is to outrage people's sense of decency, which is to shock them.

clue.text: Turn around pack animal in stream

indicators.note: turning something around faces it the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: wolves hunt in packs

explanation.surface: An instruction to a mule driver to head back along a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack animal' suggests a mule or donkey carrying loads, but here it is an animal that lives in a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Flow is a steady stream of liquid, a synonym in the noun sense.

clue.text: Enjoyment around outskirts of Tokyo, something for relaxation of Japanese

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: fun is enjoyment

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Tokyo

explanation.surface: Having fun on the edge of Tokyo, a relaxing thing for the Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese padded mattress laid on the floor, used for sleeping or lounging.

clue.text: Asian garment's bargain price — about a rupee

indicators.note: about means going round the outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: bought for a song means very cheaply
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rupee

explanation.surface: A wrap from Asia going cheaply, costing about one rupee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a song' is the idiom for a bargain price, so the price is a SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped around the waist, worn in South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Ten years Einstein transformed

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so the name's letters take a new order

parts.note: the physicist's name supplies the fodder

explanation.surface: A decade in which Einstein changed physics.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineties are a decade, the ten years from ninety to ninety-nine.

clue.text: Record-holder with advantage, right on line

indicators.note: in a list of pieces, on means placed after, so the earlier pieces follow the last one named

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
an edge is an advantage
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sports star who holds a record and has an edge on the start line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' suggests an athlete, but it is a book that holds accounts records.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is an account book in which financial records are kept.

clue.text: Spirit that's kind and friendly in the extreme

parts.note: a brand is a kind or make

indicators.note: the extreme of something is its far end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of friendly

explanation.surface: Describing someone's character as kind and extremely friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a personality, matching 'kind and friendly', but it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled liquor, and spirit is the general word for such strong drink.
